Label: ^(nozzle|print(ing)?|extrusion|extruder|hot ?end)\s*temp\w*(\s*[-(]?\s*(standard|high)\s*speed\)?)?|^nozzle(?!\s*(material|type|diameter|size))\b
Note: a sheet that prints two speeds prints two nozzle rows; the first is the standard one. A table with a temperature column names the setting alone ("Nozzle 230-260°C"), and the value must still state a temperature

Label: ^working\s+temp\w*
Note: Fillamentum's product pages print the nozzle as "Working temperature: 235–260 °C"

Label: ^printing\s+termperatures?
Note: Recreus misspells its nozzle row "Printing termperatures 215 - 225°C"

Label: ^(bed|heat ?bed|heated bed|build (plate|platform|surface)|platform|table|plate)\s*temp\w*|^heat ?bed\b
Note: a table with a temperature column names the bed alone; a sheet may call the heated bed the plate: Plate Temp.

Label: ^print(ing)?\s+(platform|bed|plate)\s*temp\w*|^(hot ?bed|build plate|printing platform)\s*temperature|^(底板|热床|平台)温度
Note: SUNLU prints the bed as "Print Platform Temp.", and a bilingual sheet labels it in Chinese; neither starts with the bed's name (data audit 2026-10-01, RC8)

Label: ^hot ?pad\b|^print(ing)?\s+bed\s+temp\w*
Note: Fillamentum prints the heated bed as "Hot pad 80–105 °C"; a control re-read of 2026-10-01 found it unread

Label: ^bottom plate temp\w*
Note: Jamg He prints the bed as "Bottom plate temperature 45-60 ºC" (not Eryone's "Bottom printing temperature", the first layer's nozzle)

Label: ^(recommended\s+)?environment(al)?\s+temp\w*
Note: Polymaker prints "Recommended environmental temperature Room temperature - 45 (˚C)": the air the part is printed in

Label: ^ambient\s+temp\w*(\s+for\s+printing)?
Note: Flashforge's "Ambient Temperature for Printing Room temperature~40℃"

Label: ^(closed|enclosed)\s*(chamber|space|build ?(chamber|volume))|^(chamber|enclosure|housing)
Note: a chamber statement with no temperature of its own is about the enclosure

Label: ^closure\s+chamber\b|^compatible\s+printer\s+type\b|^-?\s*seal\s+the\s+box\b
Note: Polymaker's row "Closure chamber | Not needed" (or "Needed (100-110°C)"); a table's "Compatible Printer Type | Enclosed-frame" and SIDDAMENT's "Seal the Box: No" (2026-10-02)

Label: ^room temp\.?(?!\w)
Note: SUNLU's table row "Room Temp. | Room Temperature": the temperature the printer stands in

Label: ^extruder\s*[:：]
Note: 3D-Fuel prints the nozzle as "Extruder: 240 - 260ºC" (the profile root-cause sweep of 2026-10-02)

Label: ^bed\s*[:：]|^heizbett(temperatur)?\b|^recommended\s+heat\s*bed\s+temp\w*(\s+to\s+print\s+[^:]{1,40}:)?
Note: 3D-Fuel's "Bed: 100 - 110ºC", purefil's German "Heizbett Temperatur" and 3DJake's "Recommended heat bed temperature to print …" (2026-10-02)

Label: ^blast\s+drying\s+oven\b|^dring\s+conditions?\b|^pre-?printing\s+drying(\s+conditions)?\b
Note: Bambu Lab's and Kingroon's "Blast Drying Oven: 80 °C, 8 h", eSUN's misspelt "Dring Conditions" and CreatBot's "Pre-printing Drying Conditions" (2026-10-02)

Label: ^compatible\s+nozzle\s+material\b|^(using\s+)?(an?\s+)?abrasion[- ]resist\w*\s+nozzle\b
Note: IPCON's "Compatible Nozzle Material Any common material" and Raise3D's "Using abrasion resistance nozzle, such as hardened steel …" (2026-10-02)

Label: ^(build plate|print(ing)? (surface|plate)|bed surface|plate)\s*(material|treatment|surface)?\b
Note: the row may name what the plate is made of or what it is coated with: Plate Material / Plate Treatment

Label: ^(drying|dry)\s*(temp\w*|conditions|settings|parameters|recommendations|preparation)|^dry(ing)? before
Note: a sheet may abbreviate it: Drying Temp.

Label: ^trocknungs(temperatur|bedingungen)\b
Note: the same row on a German sheet

Label: ^(ruby or hardened nozzle|hardened nozzle|hardened steel or ruby|abrasion[- ]resistant nozzle|nozzle (type|material))
Note: 'Abrasion resistance' is a measured property (ISO 4649), not a statement about the nozzle

Label: ^l(ü|ue)ftergeschwindigkeit\b|^bauteilk(ü|ue)hlung\b
Note: the same row on a German sheet

Label: ^(print(ing)? )?speed|^(max\.?|maximum)?\s*volumetric\s*(flow\s*)?(speed|rate)?
Note: a maximum volumetric speed is a limit on the print speed and the register keeps it as speed guidance

Label: ^druckgeschwindigkeit\b
Note: the same row on a German sheet
